Quick readout from the canary (detailed numbers attached in CSV):
- Workload: short-chat prompts (avg req length 40 tokens, max 256)
- Model variant: redwood-13b-v2-8bit (dedicated pool, us-west2, 1k warm sessions)
- P50 latency (inference-only): 120 ms
- P95 latency (inference-only): 480 ms
- End-to-end P95 (client->response): 560 ms (includes ~60ms network + 20ms queuing)
- Peak throughput observed: 220 reqs/sec sustained across the pool (autoscale events suppressed for canary)
- KV cache hit-rate: 24% (prefix reuse), which reduced token compute by ~8%
- Token throughput: ~3200 tokens/sec GPU aggregate
- Errors: transient 503 spike during a small scheduling window (~0.6% of requests)

Interpretation / risk: P95 inference is marginally above our stated MAP gate (450ms). The majority of the delta (~30–40ms) appears to be model-side tail latencies and some queuing when prefix batching aligns. Network and queuing contribute the remainder.

Proposed immediate tuning steps (with owners & ETA):
1) Canary a micro-batching change: increase batch window to 30ms for this pool to reduce tail variance — Owner: Rishi — ETA: 48 hours
2) Trial a mixed-precision kernel for the attention block (reduces per-token compute) — Owner: Monica — ETA: 72 hours
3) Temporarily raise global min instances to reduce preemption churn during peak — Owner: Marissa — ETA: 24 hours (ops change)
4) Increase KV cache warm-up (persist hot prefixes between canary runs) — Owner: Tom (Nexa) / Rishi (coord) — ETA: next run
5) Add a lightweight retry/backoff policy for the 503 spike (client-side) — Owner: Avery — ETA: 1 week

If we complete 1–3 this week and run the same canary profile, I anticipate P95 inference dropping ~40–70ms (targeting ~430ms). That would bring end-to-end P95 under 500ms with network included.

I’ll push a new canary_config.yaml to the Drive link and attach it here.

-Rishi
